correctness.rationale: Every nonzero 3x3 square-zero field reduction has rank one. For commuting such reductions AB=BA=0, and fixing A=E12 yields B=bE12+cE13+dE32 with cd=0. Four reduction strata have exact populations 1, 2S(q), S(q)(q−1), and 2q(q−1)S(q). Dual-number lifting is the linear kernel of AP+PA=0, BQ+QB=0, [A,Q]+[P,B]=0. Direct normal-form solving gives nullities 18,10,9,8 over odd characteristic, including 2h=0 forcing h=0 on proportional reductions. Summation proves C(q)=q^18+(5q−3)S(q)q^9 for all odd prime powers. Embedded standalone program exhaustively checks all base pairs and constraint ranks for F2 and F3 and representative nullities for F5/F7. The finite tests are not asserted to prove the general formula.

originality.rationale: Four relevant primary full texts and six actual research-record semantic searches were compared at statement/implication level. Prior single-matrix local-ring similarity, field-level commuting class results, and individual Jordan-lift counts do not directly imply constrained first-order ordered-pair fibers. A recorded exterior-algebra representation-scheme theorem covers characteristic two and anticommutation; the present statement excludes characteristic two and establishes an odd-characteristic proportional-stratum nullity of nine instead of ten. Potential unlocated specialized pair-enumeration literature remains a risk.

value.rationale: The natural three-dimensional representation problem for the commutative two-generator square-zero algebra acquires a first-order extension over finite dual numbers. Dimension three is the smallest size in which independent nonzero commuting square-zero field reductions appear, so stratifying the complete pair scheme is structurally motivated. A closed formula for all odd prime powers and its four affine fiber dimensions establish an exact nontrivial deformation invariant; the dimension-nine proportional stratum sharply distinguishes commuting and anticommuting deformation theories. It is not an arbitrary finite census or mere relabeling.
